# SD13-E5 Barbarian level 10 FIVE-rage-power fixture: the level-10 chassis
# fixture plus all five PF1 CRB rage power selections (slots at barbarian
# levels 2/4/6/8/10 per "Starting at 2nd level, a barbarian gains a rage
# power. She gains another rage power for every two levels of barbarian
# attained after 2nd level."), each a distinct power honoring "a barbarian
# cannot select an individual power more than once." Chosen input only via
# the open-ended numbered-slot idiom; no power's effect is computed and the
# rage-state execution engine stays the named engine burden.
# SD13-E5 deterministic Human Barbarian level 10 progression fixture.
# Widens the accepted SD13-E3/E5 deterministic PF1 Core Rulebook Human
# Barbarian level-1..level-9 martial chassis baseline to level 10 as chosen
# input only. It names selections; it does not contain derived, computed, or
# parity values. It preserves the accepted Human race-choice seam
# (ability-bonus and bonus-feat) and the deterministic
# ability/feat/skill/equipment posture from the level-1 through level-9
# fixtures, adding only the level bump this bounded tranche needs. No
# rage-power choice-slot line is present (rage powers are a
# level-2/4/6/8/10 choice-list feature this tranche deliberately does not
# implement — a genuinely open-ended power list, not a flat arithmetic
# burden; 10th IS a rage-power level, but exactly like the 2/4/6/8 grants
# before it the selection stays named-but-unproven), so no new choice=
# line is required beyond the level-1..level-9 baseline.
#
# It deliberately avoids every later Barbarian burden surface: no rage
# execution (activation, round tracking, fatigue), no rage-power
# recognition or execution, no damage-reduction application engine, and no
# level-11+ progression. The PF1 Core Rulebook Barbarian class table's
# level-10 "Special" column reads "Damage reduction 2/—, rage power"
# (verified independently against d20pfsrd and legacy.aonprd.com) — the DR
# entry is a tier-rise on the already-grounded Damage Reduction
# flat-magnitude pillar (1 at 7th, rising by 1 at 10th and every three
# levels thereafter), and the rage-power entry is the same open-ended
# choice-list feature left unproven at 2/4/6/8 — so no new pillar is
# grounded at level 10, only the existing pillars are widened.
